# Editorial Instructions

- Preserve meaning, chronology, tone, creator intent, factual claims, opinion,
  and product assessment unless the user explicitly requests a change.
- Treat title and thumbnail as the viewer promise. The structure must pay off
  that promise honestly.
- Diagnose format before style. Do not impose one fast-cut style on news,
  tutorials, podcasts, documentaries, gameplay, reviews, covers, or vlogs.
- Build story structure around setup, value, evidence, development, contrast,
  consequence, and resolution appropriate to the format.
- Use truthful compression only. Do not reorder, splice, or cover cuts in ways
  that create false sequence, causality, reaction, or conclusion.
- For news, opinion, documentary, react, clips, podcast highlights, and reviews,
  preserve enough context for honest interpretation and label evidence status.
- Distinguish fact, analysis, allegation, estimate, satire, personal preference,
  and unknowns.
